quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar strong material. This gives you the best grip and protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph. These include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on riding your motorcycle and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Stay out of the blind spots of large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a motorcycle rider has an advantage over a car driver because:

options.text: The motorcycle can accelerate faster than a car.
The motorcycle rider can use the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle rider can use the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles on your right, ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between cars. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.explanation: Look through every turn by turning only your head. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Do not turn your shoulders.

questions.question: If you have only one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. Do not ride if you have consumed any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases the risk of hitting them. Riding on the far side may cause them to return too soon.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.explanation: Passengers should always sit behind the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist or hips. If the motorcycle has handgrips, they can hold those instead. Never sit sidesaddle.

questions.question: To stop quickly on wet pavement, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes if you need to stop quickly on a slippery surface. Apply the front brake slowly to avoid locking the wheel.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear reflective clothing even in daylight to stay visible. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a sudden power change during the turn.
Keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a sudden power change during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before starting a turn. Shifting gears during a turn can cause a sudden power change to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, shift smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can get a better view of the uneven surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: You should inspect your motorcycle for safety:
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before riding. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: Which footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Laced-up boots are best. If your boots have long laces, tuck them away securely before riding.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your ability to ride safely?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can reduce your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of a small vehicle like a motorcycle. Do not assume that other drivers understand your speed and location.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should continually scan the road ahead for:
questions.explanation: Scan ahead for changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and escape routes. Be ready to react to any changes.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when towing a trailer. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What is the best way to change gears when entering a turn?

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: How should you change gears when slowing or stopping a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Why is stopping in a turn difficult?

options.text: The bike is leaning, so there is less grip available for stopping.
The rider is focused on the turn and not on braking.
The brakes do not work while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bike is leaning, so there is less grip available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be careful. While the motorcycle is leaning to turn, some grip is used for the turn. This leaves less grip for stopping.

questions.question: Which brake is stronger on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does it feel like if your front tire goes flat?
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when stopping?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly.

questions.question: What must you do when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit to complete the pass.
You can ignore no passing zone markings if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must stay within the posted speed limit and only happen in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of a crash between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of crashes between motorcycles and other vehicles. The biggest danger is when a car turns left in front of a motorcycle.
